what: Tools with no static one-hop inbound link from any sibling tool. Read by `node platform/pages/siblings.mjs --check` and by siblings.test.mjs. A ratchet, not a target: LOWER it in the same commit that closes a pair, so a new tool shipping with no sibling link turns a run red instead of waiting to be noticed. Raising it is a deliberate act that belongs in a pull request body with a reason.
why:
Measured 197 tools, 164 of them reachable from another tool only by walking back up to a category index. The related-tool strip rotates alphabetically inside a subcategory, so on a large subcategory a pair may never appear on each other's page. Fifteen commits between 2026-09-02 and 2026-09-07 each closed exactly one such pair, every one found by a session happening to notice it -- two of them (#3718, #3723) landed while this tool was being written, and #3723 closed the asphalt pave/sealcoat pair the first report named. That is the argument for the tool rather than against it: the work was already being done, one pair at a time, off a worklist nobody had.

Raised from 33 to 34 on 2026-09-08: `ats-resume-checker` graduated as a genuinely new niche (job seekers, ATS-format checking) with no existing sibling tool in the portfolio to link -- there is nothing yet to pair it with, so it is a real orphan rather than a missed link. Lower this back once a second job-seeker-facing tool ships and the two are cross-linked.

Lowered from 34 to 32 on 2026-09-08: closed the tiktok-shop-fee-calculator / walmart-marketplace-calculator pair -- both were only linked from marketplace-fee-compare, a shared hub, not from each other directly, so a crawler landing on either marketplace-take-rate calculator could never reach the other in one hop. Each page's footer now names the other, with a page.test.mjs assertion on the href.

Raised 32 -> 33 (214 -> 215 tools) the same day, merging concurrently with the above: `certified-payroll-calculator` graduated as a genuinely new niche (Davis-Bacon payroll compliance) with no existing topical sibling in the fleet to link -- forcing a link to an unrelated tool just to close the budget would defeat the point of the check, so the honest move is to raise the ceiling by exactly one rather than fabricate a pairing. Lower this back once a second Davis-Bacon/certified-payroll tool ships and the two are cross-linked.

Lowered from 33 to 32 on 2026-09-08: closed the certified-payroll-calculator orphan against `contractor-bid-readiness` rather than leaving the budget raised for it. The raise was the right call in the merge that shipped the venture -- nothing existed to pair it with at a glance -- but the pair is real on a second look: a contractor pursuing the public work that carries a wage determination is the same person who inherits the Davis-Bacon payroll obligation after the award, so the two tools sit either side of one workflow. Each page's footer now names the other, with a page.test.mjs assertion on the href.

Lowered from 32 to 31 (215 -> 216 tools) on 2026-09-08: `ios-privacy-manifest-check` graduated -- a browser-local and CLI checker for iOS developers, same shape as the CI-checks family but for Apple's Required Reason API / PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy rather than an npm or Actions artifact. It also picked up its own missed pairing: `dependency-confusion-check` (graduated the same day) had no inbound sibling link either, only outbound ones, so it was already an uncounted orphan before this tool's slug even existed. Cross-linking the two closed both at once -- 33 measured with the new tool unlinked, 31 after. Each page's footer now names the other, with a page.test.mjs assertion on the href in both ventures.

Lowered from 31 to 30 (216 -> 221 tools) on 2026-09-09: `env-example-drift-check` graduated -- a browser-local and CLI checker diffing an .env.example file against the environment variables a repo's own source code actually reads, same deterministic no-network shape as `structured-data-drift-check`. Cross-linked the two in the same commit (structured-data-drift-check's footer already named a sibling checker, `ai-crawler-access-check`; this adds a second) rather than shipping the new tool as an orphan first and closing it later. Each page's footer now names the other, with a page.test.mjs assertion on the href in both ventures.

Held at 30 (221 -> 222 tools) on 2026-09-09, the same day: `package-exports-drift-check` graduated -- a browser-local and CLI checker for a package.json `exports` map's literal targets against the files that actually exist, same deterministic no-network shape as `env-example-drift-check` and `structured-data-drift-check`. Its own footer links both of those siblings, and `env-example-drift-check`'s footer was extended in the same commit to name it back, so the new tool shipped with an inbound sibling link from its first commit rather than landing as a 31st orphan to close later.

Raised from 30 to 31 (222 -> 223 tools) on 2026-09-09: `affiliate-disclosure-checker` graduated -- a browser-local and CLI checker for bloggers/content creators, a genuinely different vertical from every other checker in the fleet (those all serve a developer checking a repo artifact; this serves a content creator checking their own published page against an affiliate-disclosure requirement) and filed under `solo-earner` by audience rather than under the CI-checks family by shape. Nothing existing pairs with it topically -- forcing a link to an unrelated tool just to close the budget would defeat the point of the check, so the honest move is to raise the ceiling by exactly one rather than fabricate a pairing, same call made for `ats-resume-checker` and `certified-payroll-calculator` above. Lower this back once a second content-creator-monetization tool ships and the two are cross-linked.
